ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every proposed shareholder, director, supervisor, beneficial owner and authorized signatory against: (i) Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission PEP and sanctioned-entity registers; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN); (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; and (v) PRC Ministry of Public Security sanctions and judicial-foreigner restriction lists. Any PEP match requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds documentation, and senior-management approval before filing. Any sanctions hit requires immediate deferral of incorporation and a mandatory report to Taiwan's Financial Intelligence Unit (Investigation Bureau, Ministry of Justice) within 48 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) 'Company and Commerce One-Stop Online Application Portal' (公司與商業一站式線上申請作業系統) at https://onestop.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Traditional Chinese characters and must include a company-type designation: Limited Company (有限公司) or Company Limited by Shares (股份有限公司). A romanized English transliteration may be registered as an alternative name but has no controlling legal effect. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company name or trademark in the same industry, and must not violate cross-strait naming restrictions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 政府/國家/中華民國/臺灣 (Government/National/R.O.C./Taiwan within a commercial name)
金融科技 (Financial Technology) where implying supervised activity
大陸或中國 (Mainland China or China) where creating cross-strait ambiguity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the MOEA rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the Department of Commercial Services within 30 days of the rejection notice, distinguishing the name from the conflicting identifier. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (訴願) with the Executive Yuan under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of such denial. During pendency, no parallel name application for the same entity may be filed; a fresh name pre-check may be re-submitted at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk MarTech/Analytics SaaS entity, a virtual office is permissible if the service provider is commercially registered in Taiwan, provides a physical local address for service of process, and is not a mere post-office box. The registered office must appear on the company registration and support the ability to receive official correspondence. MOEA practice requires a lease or service agreement evidencing address control.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low: approximate 5% annual base probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for a standard low-risk SaaS company; increased to 10–12% during the first 12 months following incorporation if the sole local address is a virtual office without identifiable business substance, or where the PRC beneficial owner has no physical presence in Taiwan.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 128-137, 156, 171-173, 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 6-10; Rules Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Chinese.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部), Department of Company Registration; Investment Commission for foreign-owned capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form (公司設立登記申請書) with attached Articles of Incorporation and supporting certification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum capital for general IT services; the full intended paid-up capital must be subscribed and deposited in a bank escrow account. The Investment Commission may require capital adequacy evidence for foreign investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the initial meeting held on [date], the board unanimously resolved as follows: 1. The Articles of Incorporation submitted to the registration authority are hereby adopted. 2. The subscription of [number] ordinary shares by each founding shareholder is approved, and the paid-up capital deposited in the escrow bank account is confirmed. 3. The address at [address] is adopted as the registered office and legal seat. 4. [Name] is appointed as General Manager with authority to run day-to-day operations; [Name] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer with authority to open bank accounts and file tax declarations. 5. The incorporation application and all related formalities are authorized to proceed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Department of Company Registration (online name portal) and Investment Commission for foreign investment approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the MOEA company name reservation portal and submit the desired Chinese and English corporate names, business scope, and shareholder structure. For foreign shareholders, concurrently file a preliminary investment application with the Investment Commission to obtain approval under the Foreign Investment Act before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Passport or certificate of incorporation of each foreign shareholder
Business plan and investment scope description
Financial statements or solvency evidence of the foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, re-submit with up to five alternative names within 14 days. If the Investment Commission issues a query, provide supplementary corporate and financial documentation; appeal any adverse determination within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Establishment Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed in Taiwan, or qualified corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and notarize the Articles of Incorporation defining authorized capital, share classes, voting rights, and governance procedures. Convene an establishment meeting of all subscribers to approve the Articles, elect directors and statutory supervisors, and record the resolutions in minutes.
required_dossiers: Written consent of nominees for directors and supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any notarization errors or missing consents within 7 days; hold a supplementary meeting if the original minutes are legally defective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Bank Escrow Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank and Foreign Exchange Department, Central Bank of Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital collection account at a licensed bank; remit the full paid-up capital from shareholders. Obtain a bank capital certificate confirming receipt of funds and a foreign exchange remittance certificate if the funds originate abroad. Verify the legitimate source of capital with supporting documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or Central Bank questions the provenance of funds, submit additional anti-money laundering or source-of-wealth documents. In case of delay, request a written explanation and expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration with Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Company Registration (company online registration system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Company Incorporation Registration Application Form online, attaching the notarized Articles, bank capital certificate, establishment meeting minutes, consents of directors/supervisors, and the investment approval letter. Pay the official fee (NT$1,000) and await issuance of the Company Registration Certificate (establishment notice).
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form (公司設立登記申請書)
Identity documents of directors and supervisors
Proof of registered office (lease or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for correction, cure the stated deficiencies within 15 statutory days and resubmit. If rejected, address the grounds and file a new application once the defects are cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification with National Taxation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (local regional bureau)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, register as a taxpayer and obtain the Unified Business Number (tax ID) by filing the Business Registration Application with the local National Taxation Bureau. Submit the incorporation certificate, lease evidence, responsible person ID, and seal. This step activates VAT and income tax status for company operations.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Application Form (營利事業登記)
Registered office lease or property ownership certificate
Responsible person's national ID and company seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documents are incomplete, the tax authority allows a 7-day rectification window. Failure to register may incur late filing penalties; appeal within 30 days if the tax authority determines a different registration zone.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Labor Insurance, Health Insurance, and Pension Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration; Ministry of Labor (workplace inspection division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer with the labor insurance and national health insurance systems, and enroll all employees in the labor pension plan within 8 days of their start date. Complete enrollment forms with employee personal data and work contracts. If foreign employees will be engaged, apply for their work permits.
required_dossiers: Work permit applications for foreign staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late enrollment is remedied by immediate filing and payment of penalties; work permit queries are responded to with rental and salary evidence; administrative appeal available within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office Premises Safety and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal building authority; fire department; Occupational Safety and Health Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a building safety inspection for the registered office to confirm the space complies with the Building Act and local zoning. Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate and, if necessary, a structure occupancy permit. Labor authorities may perform a workplace safety clearance, focusing on electrical, HVAC, and emergency exits, but no special industrial license is required for a software/analytics service.
required_dossiers: Building use permit or occupancy approval application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire or building inspection identifies deficiencies, complete all corrective works and re-inspect within 10 days. Once the certificate is issued, retain a copy for government audits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), or solid industrial waste are generated. Office waste is limited to general municipal waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire department, building use/load inspection certificate from the municipal building authority, and workplace labor safety inspection clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (Ministry of Labor).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of China (Taiwan), administered through the competent local National Taxation Bureau; the principal electronic tax portal is the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw). Company and foreign-company registration is generally coordinated with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, and the local tax bureau.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Taiwan company or Taiwan-registered Sino-foreign equity joint venture must first complete company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the competent local authority, obtain its eight-digit Uniform Business Number (統一編號), and complete tax registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable business. A foreign company establishing a branch or other fixed business presence must obtain approval and registration under the Company Act, receive a Uniform Business Number, and register for business tax. A foreign enterprise without a Taiwan establishment that supplies cross-border electronic services to Taiwan consumers may be required to register for VAT through the designated online tax-registration process and obtain a tax identification number when the statutory registration threshold is met. Applications generally require constitutional documents, certificate of incorporation, responsible-person identification, Taiwan agent or representative information, registered-address evidence, business scope, bank information where requested, and certified Chinese translations or notarization/legalization where applicable. Registration should be completed before taxable operations or invoice issuance. A separate VAT number is generally not issued in the European Union format; the Uniform Business Number and tax-registration status are the principal Taiwan identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election for ordinary companies, branches, or equity joint ventures. A Taiwan company is generally subject to profit-seeking enterprise income tax at entity level, with dividends or profit distributions potentially subject to separate shareholder-level consequences. A taxpayer generally cannot elect partnership or transparent treatment merely by filing a tax form. Business-tax treatment is determined by the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Tax Act, the nature and place of supply, and the taxpayer's registration status. Taiwan has targeted anti-avoidance and controlled-foreign-company rules, but no broad statutory hybrid-mismatch election that converts an ordinary Taiwan limited company into a pass-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Tax, commonly referred to as Taiwan VAT or business tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For ordinary business-tax registration, the commonly applied monthly sales thresholds are NT$80,000 for sellers of goods and NT$40,000 for providers of services, subject to statutory exclusions, changes in law, and the tax authority's classification. For foreign enterprises supplying electronic services to Taiwan individuals, the relevant registration threshold is generally annual Taiwan-source sales of NT$480,000. A business may be required to register earlier where it has a fixed place of business, taxable operations, or another statutory registration trigger. A Taiwan company or registered branch should not rely on the small-business threshold to postpone registration without confirmation from the competent National Taxation Bureau.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses a government-regulated electronic invoice system administered by the Ministry of Finance. Businesses subject to electronic-invoice requirements must issue compliant electronic invoices, use an approved service provider or compatible system, assign compliant invoice numbers, retain transaction data, and transmit invoice information to the Ministry of Finance electronic invoice platform within the applicable statutory timing. Taiwan generally does not operate a universal pre-issuance real-time clearance model equivalent to China's Golden Tax system; transmission and platform validation occur under the electronic-invoice rules. B2B invoices, B2C electronic invoices, carrier or cloud-invoice arrangements, and donation or buyer-identification data have separate technical requirements. Paper invoices remain available in permitted circumstances, but businesses should confirm applicability, transmission deadlines, XML specifications, certificate requirements, and system onboarding with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing SaaS sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Taiwan business-tax rules, exported goods may qualify for a 0% rate when the goods are exported from Taiwan and the export is supported by customs records. Services may qualify for 0% treatment where they are supplied to foreign customers and are used or enjoyed outside Taiwan, including qualifying offshore services, provided the statutory place-of-use and evidentiary requirements are met. For a MarTech analytics SaaS business, zero rating is not automatic merely because the customer is incorporated abroad: the supplier should establish the customer's foreign status, contractual recipient, service-use location, delivery and access records, absence of Taiwan use or benefit where required, invoice trail, and receipt of consideration through acceptable banking or foreign-exchange evidence. Services supplied to Taiwan customers or used in Taiwan generally remain subject to 5% VAT. VAT refunds or credits for export transactions require properly documented input tax, valid invoices, business-tax filings, and proof supporting the 0% output treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs export declaration or equivalent customs export record for exported goods
Commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and Bill of Lading or air waybill where applicable
Foreign customer contract, purchase order, service agreement, or platform order record
Evidence identifying the foreign customer and the contractual recipient
Electronic service delivery, access, usage, or system-log evidence supporting offshore use where relevant
Bank remittance advice, foreign-exchange settlement record, or other legally acceptable evidence of receipt of export proceeds
Taiwan business-tax invoice and sales ledger showing the 0% transaction
Proof of import-country delivery or acceptance for goods, where required by the tax authority
Tax return schedules and supporting reconciliation between accounting revenue, customs data, invoices, and bank receipts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 180-day period is a commonly applied foreign-exchange remittance benchmark for export proceeds and must be checked against the transaction type, applicable foreign-exchange rules, banking requirements, and any approved extension; it is not a universal VAT rule for every offshore service. The National Taxation Bureau may deny or reverse 0% treatment where export, offshore use, foreign-customer status, or payment evidence is insufficient. The resulting VAT may be assessed retroactively at 5%, together with interest, late-payment charges, and administrative penalties. Incorrect invoices, false customs or remittance evidence, omitted sales, or intentional use of 0% treatment to evade tax may trigger penalties under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Tax Act, potentially including fines calculated by reference to the evaded tax, loss of refund or credit entitlement, and criminal exposure for serious tax fraud or document falsification. Records should generally be retained for the statutory tax-preservation period and longer where an audit, refund claim, litigation, or customs matter remains open.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Basic Information Declaration (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May; MOEA’s online filing platform opens on 1 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA serves a formal warning and imposes an administrative fine of NT$10,000; continued failure to correct during the following year may lead to MOEA-initiated dissolution or administrative strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the fiscal year end; extended to 30 June if a certified public accountant or tax agent is engaged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% on the underpaid tax (minimum NT$1,500), plus monthly arrears interest of 3% on the tax shortfall; sustained non-compliance triggers compulsory collection, freezing of bank accounts, and travel restrictions on responsible persons

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of Annual Business Report and Financial Statements by Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders’ Meeting; minutes and board resolutions retained in the statutory Minute Book and available to MOEA upon inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary shareholders’ meeting must be convened by 30 June after the fiscal year end, within six months of the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are jointly and severally subject to an MOEA administrative fine of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; failure to obtain shareholder approval blocks lawful dividend distributions and may expose the company to shareholder remedies such as a shareholder-convened extraordinary meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June after the fiscal year end, covering remittance flows, business operation, and any shareholding changes involving the foreign JV shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning or suspension of foreign-investment approval benefits; a record of delinquency can delay or block future dividend remittance, capital repatriation, and equity transfer applications by the foreign JV partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit and attestation is required under Company Act Article 20(3) where paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million; the audit is also mandatory for TWSE/TPEx-listed companies, financial institutions, and other enterprises designated by the Financial Supervisory Commission. A low-capital MarTech/SEO software JV is not statutorily audited unless the paid-in capital threshold is exceeded or investor covenants require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public-interest entities apply Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) as endorsed by the FSC; non-public enterprises apply the ROC Business Entity Accounting Act and its related accounting rules (ROC GAAP). Tax records and vouchers must be retained for at least seven years, while commercial ledgers and financial statements under the Business Entity Accounting Act must be retained for ten years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, through the MOEA online declaration, the company must confirm and update the identities, nationalities, and shareholding percentages of directors, supervisors, managers, and all shareholders holding 10% or more. Any share transfer producing or extinguishing a 10%+ shareholding during the year must be reflected in the immediately following annual declaration, while the internal shareholders register must be updated at the effective date of the transfer. This same declaration serves as the annual beneficial-ownership confirmation for non-public companies in Taiwan.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800–1,500 annual registered address, statutory mail handling, and corporate secretarial coordination in Taipei or Hsinchu
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–9,000 for a ROC GAAP certified audit when triggered; no audit fee is required if paid-in capital remains below NT$30 million and no shareholder or investment-approval covenant mandates an audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general sectoral tax holiday for software or MarTech SaaS entities. The JV may use the R&D investment tax credit equal to 15% of qualifying research and development expenditures, capped at 30% of the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax payable, as well as investment tax credits for smart machinery and 5G equipment. Software development costs are amortizable over five years. Undistributed earnings exceeding permitted retained earnings thresholds attract a 5% retained earnings surtax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance e-Filing system (電子申報繳稅服務, tax.nat.gov.tw)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within five months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year JV, the statutory filing period is 1 May through 31 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales revenue including SaaS subscriptions, SEO analytics license fees, data crawler service fees, and advertising-supported data product income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must ensure all Taiwan-source revenue generated through Stripe or Paddle payment rails is fully declared; inaccurately routing Taiwan-origin online subscription income offshore will trigger reclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to software development, cloud hosting, data center operations, and content crawler infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only when supported by invoices and contemporaneous documentation; related-party charges paid to the mainland parent must satisfy the arm's length requirement under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains, sublicensing royalties, and residual maintenance payments from overseas analytics customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Taiwan-source and worldwide income of the Taiwanese resident JV must be declared; royalties subsequently paid to a non-resident parent become separately subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted to taxable income, applying the five-year loss carryforward, non-deductible expenses, and income tax credit limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any non-documented related-party management fees, imputed interest, or artificial intercompany deductibles to derive the correct taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax computation, net of foreign tax credits, prepayments, and eligible investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend withholding tax due on distributions to the non-resident shareholder is a separate remittance obligation and must be withheld when the distribution resolution is implemented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable cause attracts an additional tax of 15% of the underpaid amount plus daily interest at the central bank discount rate. Deliberate false declaration or concealment under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act triggers a penalty of 0.5 to 3 times the evaded tax; fraudulent evasion under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act carries criminal liability including imprisonment up to five years and fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation is signed but not currently in force; therefore, dividends from the TW JV to a People's Republic of China parent remain subject to the statutory 21% withholding unless restructuring through a jurisdiction with a fully ratified Taiwan DTA is implemented. For an in-force tax treaty, the beneficial owner must file the Treaty Withholding Rate Application with the National Taxation Bureau, attach the home jurisdiction Certificate of Residence (TRC), current audited financial statements, and a sworn beneficial ownership declaration, and obtain approval before applying the reduced withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates are 20% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to non-residents. Under an in-force DTA these rates may be reduced to 10% or lower, strictly subject to submission of a valid TRC, compliance with the limitation on benefits clause, and the absence of routed-agent arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Transfer Pricing Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transaction amounts exceed NT$50 million. A Master File is required when the consolidated group revenue of the multinational group exceeds NT$50 billion. Below the threshold, the taxpayer must complete the related-party disclosure schedule in the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and be prepared to substantiate the arm's length nature of all cross-border transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations code comparable to the UAE; however, the competent tax authority applies the substance-over-form principle, Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act, and beneficial ownership clauses in DTAs to deny treaty benefits or reallocate income where the JV lacks payroll, premises, management functions, or substantive decision-making. Taiwan's CFC rules introduced in 2021 further require an actual active business presence before deferral of income through low-tax offshore vehicles is permitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a corporate return that conceals online SaaS subscription revenue collected through Stripe or Paddle, or overstating cloud and development costs through a shell service provider controlled by the mainland parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Omitted tax assessment plus a penalty of 0.5 to 3 times the evaded tax; interest accrual; criminal fines and imprisonment up to five years under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally use the corporate form to commit fraud are exposed to veil piercing under Company Act Article 154(2) and become jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties, with potential travel restrictions under Tax Collection Act Article 24 and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan JV without physical office space, employees, network infrastructure, or actual management; using the entity solely as an invoicing nexus to shift intellectual property income from the mainland parent or offshore affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of taxable profits to the true economic owner under Article 43-1, disallowance of intercompany service fee deductions, back-tax assessments, late interest, and administrative fines for false accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the shell arrangement is deemed a sham, directors may be held jointly liable for the full enterprise tax exposure, be subjected to non-departure orders, and suffer personal asset seizure when the corporate veil is pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into royalty, software license, data analytics, or management-fee agreements with cross-border affiliated entities without any economic analysis, benchmark study, or contemporaneous local file documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustments increasing taxable income, a penalty of up to 3 times the resulting tax under Article 110, interest computations, and the risk of secondary adjustment on deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign untrue pricing certifications or knowingly direct artificial pricing practices may be personally assessed for negligence or fraud, with personal restitution and criminal exposure under commercial false-document statutes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-volume cross-border SaaS payments through Stripe or Paddle without performing adequate customer due diligence, beneficial ownership screening, or suspicious transaction reporting for unidentified overseas users.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines under the Money Laundering Control Act ranging from NT$500,000 to NT$10,000,000 per violation, mandatory internal control remediation, and potential suspension of non-banking financial service operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A responsible person who willfully disregards AML obligations may be criminally prosecuted, subjected to substantial personal fines, prohibited from leaving Taiwan during investigation, and held civilly liable for losses arising from enabled financial crime.
